name: Nirosta Steel
label: ULYSSA
lede: Steven Hall sang harmonies for Arthur Russell in the '70s, then kept his own tapes for forty years. At 69 a double LP built from them gets a 9.0 from Pitchfork.

eras.title: From a Glasgow choir to the Poets' Building
eras.text: Hall reaches America as a teenager and lands in the East Village poetry scene, where Allen Ginsberg points him at the composer who becomes his teacher.

years.h: Steven Hall starts in a Milngavie church choir, with bagpipes on the side
years.p: Born outside Glasgow, he adds French horn, then guitar. His father, an optician, dies when Hall is about eleven or twelve.
years.xp:
Tone Glow's profile says Hall's mother remarried an American she met through personal ads, and the family moved to Delaware when he was fifteen. At a liberal high school there, visiting New York poets gave him the idea of joining them.

Bad Arts describes the move differently, as a move to New York City with his widowed mother. Either way he was in the East Village poetry world as a teenager.

years.h: A teenager walks into the Poets' Building and picks his teacher
years.p: At sixteen or seventeen Hall climbs to 437 East 12th Street, where Allen Ginsberg introduces him to [[Arthur Russell|f43370e3-6d86-44e7-ae4c-ca098962dcd0]]. Hall decides on the spot that Russell is his teacher.
years.xp:
Tone Glow's profile places Richard Hell on the second floor and Rene Ricard, a Warhol figure who was Hall's boyfriend, on the fifth. At Columbia he held editorial posts at the Poetry Project's magazine and the Columbia Review, and co-founded an arts magazine, Shiny.

He also studied at Naropa in Colorado under Ginsberg and William Burroughs, and with the trumpeter Don Cherry, according to The Tonearm.

eras.title: Arthur's other voice
eras.text: Hall harmonizes with Russell on guitars in small downtown rooms and sings on his dance records. Russell's death in 1992 ends it.

years.cap: Arthur Russell, Tom Lee and Steven Hall at a SHINY magazine party, Doug Milford Gallery, New York
years.h: Larry Levan remixes the Loose Joints single with Hall singing on it
years.p: "Is It All Over My Face?" is a 1980 West End Records single by Arthur Russell's Loose Joints. Hall is one of the voices on it.
years.xp: Wikipedia records that the track became a New York hit through WBLS airplay and was influential on Chicago house. Hall also sang on Russell's "Tell You Today" (1983), per Tone Glow, though Wikipedia credits that record's vocals to Joyce Bowden.

years.cap: Steven Hall and Arthur Russell on stage, New York
years.h: Single takes with the disco engineer Bob Blank
years.p: Hall and Russell record acoustic tracks, and Hall says the two were locked in together. FRESH FEELING and SPECIAL WEAKNESS finally come out on MY SKYSCRAPER in 2026.
years.xp:
As The Sailboats, Hall and Russell played the Mudd Club, CBGB and Max's Kansas City, according to The Tonearm. Hall told Tone Glow that Russell sang flat in the manner of Chet Baker, with a no-vibrato rule, while he took the harmonies.

Hall also says Russell told him not to be afraid of writing something pretty, which pushed him toward writing his own songs.

years.p: Wikipedia gives the cause as AIDS-related illness. Hall forms Arthur's Landing with other friends from Russell's circle so the songs keep getting played.

eras.title: East, and then further east
eras.text: Hall drifts between New York, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Thailand, recording in Mandarin and Thai and filling the archive that becomes his own catalog.

years.h: Hall moves between Hong Kong and Taipei with producer Jim Shum
years.p: He works as assistant sound recorder on the 1993 film 18, and later records a Mandarin album with Beijing opera singer Hung Chiu Fung. Jim Shum produces.
years.xp:
Tone Glow says Hall met Shum through the Hong Kong theater group Zuni Icosahedron, who became his best friend and producer. He also played with Cantonese musicians in Kowloon's Walled City before it closed in 1993, and was cast as Lawrence of Arabia in a Mitsubishi commercial.

The Mandarin album with Hung Chiu Fung remains unreleased. Their song MOHAN is on MY SKYSCRAPER. DRY ICE, on Buddhist Army in 2017, gathers 1980s and 1990s recordings made across Hong Kong, Taipei and Bangkok, curated by Elodie Lauten.

years.h: Taipei police raid a bookstore set, then stay for all of it
years.p: Hall plays the queer Gin Gin Bookstore in 1999. The police, suspecting an orgy, sit through the whole set and laugh, per Tone Glow.
years.xp: The show became the live album Cool Fire. Hall's song TWINKLE ANGEL, per Tone Glow, samples text from porn video boxes and moaning from a Japanese boyfriend, which Shum encouraged and the boyfriend eventually approved.

years.src: Tone Glow · Bandcamp: MY SKYSCRAPER · The Bad Arts
years.h: In Bangkok at 50, Hall writes a demo for Madonna
years.p: He records with Thai musicians alongside Jim Shum, and the demo is ENGLISH PARTY, he tells Tone Glow.
years.xp:
He says he found Thai Buddhism more part of daily life than the Buddhism he had seen in Hong Kong and Taiwan, and the nights and drugs of that period fed songs like THAITITANIUM. He also cut a version of LOST IN THOUGHT with a Thai violin.

Sources differ on ENGLISH PARTY: Bandcamp and The Bad Arts place its origins in the early 1980s.

eras.title: Keeping Arthur's songs in the air
eras.text: Arthur's Landing gets a record deal, and Hall's own live tape from Taipei goes up on Bandcamp.

years.h: Hall fronts eight Russell collaborators on Arthur's Landing
years.p: The players come from Russell's Dinosaur L, Loose Joints and Sailboats days, and the record comes out on Strut. The launch party is at NUBLU in New York on January 24.
years.xp: Resident Advisor reported the twelve-track album ran from Russell's late solo work to his disco records, with some demos never officially recorded before. Hall told the site the band had played Russell's music for thirty years and never tired of it.

years.h: A friend uploads Cool Fire to Bandcamp
years.p: The 1999 Taipei live recording is out in 2014 and includes an earlier take of GO FOR THE NIGHT, the song Hall co-wrote with Russell.
years.xp: ULYSSA found Hall through that upload twelve years later.

eras.title: The record with no final version
eras.text: At 69 Hall puts out a double LP of songs from the early 1980s to 2025, and it lands as the year's best-reviewed album so far.

q: I don't want your Arthur songs, I want your songs.
years.src: Paste: The 40-year excavation · Wikipedia: My Skyscraper
years.h: ULYSSA wants Hall's own songs, not the Arthur ones
years.p: Shane Lavers of Chanel Beads points ULYSSA's Eric Deines and John Williamson to Cool Fire. Deines tells Hall what he's after.
years.xp: That is why only one track on MY SKYSCRAPER, GO FOR THE NIGHT, is a Russell co-write. Paste's interview finds Hall recently relocated to Champaign, Illinois, with his husband.

years.src: Bandcamp: MY SKYSCRAPER · Tone Glow · Paste: Nirosta Steel, 'MY SKYSCRAPER' Review
years.h: MY SKYSCRAPER puts four decades on two LPs
years.p: Seventeen tracks and 83 minutes, in several mixes and languages, with production credits including Hall, Drop Out Orchestra, Jim Shum and Arthur's Landing.
years.xp:
Bandcamp calls the songs works-forever-in-progress. The back cover includes an image that Hall's lawyer husband worried would cause distribution trouble in China; Deines said "Come and get me," per Tone Glow, and the record ships with a sticker over it.

Paste reports Hall's line on the whole thing: "It's silly and funny to be a pop star at 69."

years.big: At once an archival triumph and one of the year's most thrilling new releases.
years.src: Album of the Year · The Bad Arts · Wikipedia: My Skyscraper
yt: Realm's Album Quest on the buzz
years.p: Harry Tafoya's review, as quoted by The Bad Arts, says almost none of the songs have a single definitive version.
years.xp: Album of the Year lists Pitchfork at 90 and Paste at 100. Wikipedia lists Paste's grade as A.

years.h: Hall plays the old Pyramid Club site, then adds a third night
years.p: Night Club 101 hosts September 10 and 11, a third night goes on at September 12, and Chicago's The Hideout follows on September 18, Stereogum reported.
years.xp: Night Club 101 stands where the Pyramid Club was, and Stereogum notes Hall played there with Russell decades earlier.
